results.recommended_endpoint: Percentage of Patients Achieving ACR20 Response at Week 12
results.rationale: Consistent with FDA Guidance for Rheumatoid Arthritis and the regulatory approval pathway for baricitinib (RA-BEAM and RA-BUILD trials) and other JAK inhibitors, the ACR20 response at Week 12 is the established primary endpoint to demonstrate reduction in signs and symptoms.

The FDA Guidance for Industry on Rheumatoid Arthritis establishes ACR20 response at Week 12 as the standard primary efficacy endpoint for registrational trials, which served as the primary basis of approval for upadacitinib in the SELECT Phase 3 clinical program.

The FDA guidance for Rheumatoid Arthritis clinical trials recommends the ACR20 response rate as the gold standard primary efficacy measure for registration, which served as the primary endpoint in the pivotal AIM and ATTAIN trials for the approval of abatacept.

results.moa: IL-6 receptor alpha (IL-6Rα) antagonist monoclonal antibody
results.rationale: In accordance with FDA guidance for rheumatoid arthritis development, ACR20 at Week 24 is the established primary efficacy endpoint for registrational trials of biologics, which served as the primary clinical basis for the approval of Kevzara (sarilumab) and other IL-6 inhibitors like tocilizumab.

FDA's guidance for rheumatoid arthritis drug development and approval precedents for other JAK inhibitors (such as upadacitinib and tofacitinib) establish the ACR20 response rate at Week 12 as the standard primary efficacy endpoint for registration trials.

results.recommended_endpoint: Proportion of participants achieving a Static Physician Global Assessment (sPGA) score of 0 or 1 and a >= 2-point improvement from baseline at Week 12
results.rationale: Consistent with FDA's guidance for psoriasis drug development, a co-primary endpoint approach requiring both sPGA of 0/1 and PASI 75 at Week 12 is the regulatory standard, as demonstrated in the pivotal UNCOVER trials for Taltz.

Per FDA guidance for plaque psoriasis and the pivotal Phase 3 trials (ERASURE and FIXTURE) for secukinumab, PASI 75 response at Week 12 is the established regulatory-approved primary endpoint (often co-primary with IGA 0 or 1) to demonstrate efficacy of IL-17A antagonists.

results.moa: IL-23 p19 subunit monoclonal antibody antagonist
results.recommended_endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of IGA score of 0 or 1 (clear or almost clear) with a >= 2-grade reduction from baseline and PASI 90 at Week 16
results.rationale: FDA class-specific guidance and the pivotal VOYAGE 1 and 2 trials for guselkumab establish these co-primary endpoints as the standard regulatory requirement to demonstrate both absolute clearance (IGA) and relative magnitude of improvement (PASI 90) for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

results.moa: IL-23 p19 subunit monoclonal antibody antagonist
results.recommended_endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving a static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) score of 0 or 1 at Week 16
results.rationale: FDA's regulatory precedent for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, demonstrated in the pivotal UltIMMa-1 and UltIMMa-2 trials for risankizumab, requires the co-primary endpoint of sPGA 0/1 (clear or almost clear) and PASI 90 at Week 16 to establish clinical efficacy.

The FDA approved upadacitinib for active psoriatic arthritis based on the phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 and SELECT-PsA 2 trials, both of which utilized the proportion of patients achieving ACR20 response at Week 12 as the primary efficacy endpoint.

results.recommended_endpoint: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Responder Index 4 (SRI4) at Week 52
results.rationale: The SRI4 at Week 52 was the primary endpoint used in the pivotal BLISS-52 and BLISS-76 phase III trials for the approval of belimumab, and is the established FDA regulatory standard for demonstrating clinically meaningful reduction in SLE disease activity without worsening in any organ system.

results.moa: calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) — T cell activation suppression
results.rationale: This endpoint served as the primary basis for the FDA approval of voclosporin in the Phase 3 AURORA-1 trial, requiring composite stabilization of eGFR, reduction in proteinuria (UPCR <= 0.5 mg/mg), and low-dose corticosteroid use, which aligns with FDA guidance for evaluating therapies for lupus nephritis.

Complete Renal Response (CRR) at Week 76 is the primary endpoint for the Phase III REGENCY trial of obinutuzumab in lupus nephritis, reflecting FDA guidance that requires sustained, long-term assessment of proteinuria and stable renal function for registrational trials in this indication.

results.indication: moderately to severely active Crohn's disease
results.moa: α4β7 integrin antagonist — gut-selective lymphocyte trafficking inhibitor
results.recommended_endpoint: Clinical remission (defined as Crohn's Disease Activity Index [CDAI] score ≤ 150) at Week 6
results.rationale: This endpoint was the FDA-agreed primary outcome for the GEMINI 2 induction trial, which led to the approval of vedolizumab for moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.

results.indication: moderately to severely active Crohn's disease
results.moa: IL-12/IL-23 p40 subunit monoclonal antibody antagonist
results.rationale: In the pivotal UNITI-1 and UNITI-2 Phase 3 induction trials that led to the FDA approval of ustekinumab for Crohn's disease, the primary endpoint was clinical response at Week 6, defined as a reduction in Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) score of at least 100 points from baseline.

results.indication: moderately to severely active Crohn's disease
results.moa: IL-23 p19 subunit monoclonal antibody antagonist
results.recommended_endpoint: Proportion of participants achieving Clinical Remission and Endoscopic Response at Week 12
results.rationale: Consistent with the 2018 FDA Draft Guidance for Crohn's Disease trials and the landmark 2022 approval of risankizumab (ADVANCE and MOTIVATE trials), the FDA requires co-primary endpoints evaluating both symptomatic improvement (clinical remission by CDAI or stool frequency/abdominal pain score) and objective mucosal healing (endoscopic response by SES-CD) at the end of the 12-week induction period.

results.indication: moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis
results.rationale: In accordance with FDA draft guidance for ulcerative colitis, clinical remission defined by the 3-component Mayo score at Week 10 (induction phase) is the established registrational primary endpoint, as utilized in the pivotal True North trial leading to ozanimod's approval.

results.moa: IL-4/IL-13 receptor (IL-4Rα) antagonist — dual IL-4 and IL-13 blockade
results.recommended_endpoint: Proportion of participants with an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) and a reduction of >= 2 points from baseline at Week 16
results.rationale: FDA's guidance for atopic dermatitis drug development establishes the IGA responder rate at Week 16 as the standard primary efficacy endpoint, which served as the basis for the approval of Dupixent in its pivotal SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 trials.

results.recommended_endpoint: Proportion of subjects with Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 or 1 and a >= 2-point reduction from baseline at Week 16
results.rationale: FDA guidance for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis trials requires the primary assessment of efficacy to be based on the IGA, establishing precedent through the approval of tralokinumab (ECZTRA 1 and 2 trials) and dupilumab using this exact endpoint at Week 16.

The Annualized Relapse Rate (ARR) is the gold-standard primary endpoint accepted by the FDA for registrational trials in relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, serving as the basis of approval for ofatumumab in the ASCLEPIOS I and II trials.
